repo_grounded_facts.statement: FEMA case 26-05-2022A: additional-information letter dated 2026-09-22; the 90-day response track ends 2026-12-21. This is the response date stated by FEMA's letter — not a legal conclusion about any statutory deadline; counsel should verify deadlines independently. A LOMA has NOT been issued.

LOMA pathway rule: FEMA distinguishes natural-grade LOMA requests from requests involving fill; fill-based requests follow the LOMR-F/CLOMR-F pathway rather than a pure LOMA. Case correspondence instructs the requester to include the case number with subsequent correspondence.

Case 26-05-2022A specifically requested a recorded deed OR recorded subdivision plat with recordation data/stamp. The local tax assessor map must clearly identify the property and include a street intersection shown on the applicable FIRM panel.

FEMA MT-1 guidance identifies Community Acknowledgment Part B for some LOMA requests involving the regulatory floodway; the community official signs it. MT-1 requires condition, construction, datum, coordinates, elevation values and BFE source; elevation values are recorded to the nearest tenth of a foot.
FRE 702 (Daubert) admissibility is a legal determination made by a court — it is not a boolean computable in code. The repository explicitly forbids self-certifying compliance claims.

Professional certification boundary: TSM may check certification metadata but cannot create or substitute for the licensed professional certification (registered Professional Engineer, Indiana IC 25-31-1). The no-rise certification in the repo (docs/regulatory/loma/no-rise-certification-DRAFT.md) is an UNFILED DRAFT with an official-seal placeholder — never represent it as filed.
